chunks.title: 01 Civora User Manual
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION CIVORA Platform User Manual Comprehensive Guide to Navigation, Data Operations, and Analytics Dashboard 1. Introduction to CIVORA CIVORA is an enterprise-grade multi-project data analytics and visualization platform designed to help retail managers, executives, and data analysts extract actionable business insights from historical sales records. The system simplifies the process of aggregating raw spreadsheet data into centralized dashboard views, enabling comparison of metrics across multiple branch locations (managed stores), categories, and timeframes. 2. Access and User Registration To access CIVORA, open a web browser and navigate to the application dashboard URL (default local url: http://localhost:3000). If you are a first-time user, click on 'Register' to create an account by providing your full name, email address, password, position (defaults to Administrator), and optional contact number. User credentials are encrypted at rest using bcrypt-based hashing. 3. Project and Store Creation * Creating a Store: Once logged in, navigate to the 'Projects' page. Click 'Add Project/Store' and enter store details such as name, type, segments, location id, logo URL, tax rates, and currency code. * Implicit Store Creation: Alternatively, if you upload a CSV/Excel file containing a 'Store' column, CIVORA will automatically scan the first row and dynamically provision a new project if the store does not already exist, associating it with your user account. 4. Data Upload and Monthly Operations Data is ingested per reporting cycle (Month/Year). On the dashboard, click the 'Import Data' button. Select the target Month (e.g., January) and Year (e.g., 2024), and pick your data file (.csv or .xlsx). The platform performs auto-validation of columns and schema before processing data using an optimized Python engine. 5. Navigating the Dashboards * Global Dashboard: Access aggregate statistics across all stores, including total revenue, net revenue, total items sold, and active hubs. * Store-Specific Dashboard: Under 'Projects', click on a managed store. The screen shifts to store-level KPIs, monthly trends, regional breakdown charts, and category mix distribution. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 02 FAQ
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) Answering Common Product, Technical, and Operational Queries 1. What file types are supported for data imports? CIVORA natively supports comma-separated value files (.csv) and Microsoft Excel files (.xlsx). Ensure your sheet contains no empty rows at the top and matches the expected semantic column layout. 2. How does the system handle state and regional spelling variations? The backend utilizes a smart alias mapping JSON configuration ('state_aliases.json'). It normalizes standard variations (e.g., 'Tamilnadu', 'TN', 'Tamil Nadu' will all be canonicalized to 'Tamil Nadu'). If a region cannot be matched, it falls back to title casing the name. 3. I uploaded data but my charts did not update. What should I do? * Check import period: Ensure you selected the correct month and year. The dashboard defaults to the year 2024; verify if your imported year matches the selected year filter. * Page refresh: Sometimes browser state updates require a manual refresh. Click F5 or reload the dashboard. * Server processing time: Depending on database volume, processing files may take between 2 to 5 seconds. Wait for the success notification in the top-right. 4. Can I host CIVORA on-premise without an active internet connection? Yes. CIVORA runs fully containerized via Docker. You can deploy it locally. However, advanced AI features that call Watsonx Orchestrate require external internet connectivity to reach the APIs. Local fallbacks for reporting will still operate offline. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 03 Data Upload Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Data Upload Guide Step-by-Step Data Preparation, Mapping, and Ingestion Workflows 1. Preparing the Source File Your uploaded files must represent sales data for a single calendar month. Files can contain granular rows (individual sales transactions) or pre-aggregated figures grouped by product and region. Avoid formatting numbers with commas or currency symbols (e.g., use '50000', not '$50,000'). 2. Required Columns & Formats * Date: Values must conform to YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-01-15'). * Category: Category classification, such as Electronics, Furniture, Appliances, Fashion, Groceries, Books, or Stationery. * Region: The location or Indian state name (e.g., Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi). * Revenue: Total sales revenue in numeric format (retains up to 2 decimal places). * Cost: Total operating cost of the item to determine profit margins. * Quantity: The number of units sold (integer). 3. The Ingestion Pipeline 1. Upload: Click the 'Import Data' action in the header bar. 2. Mapping screen: If your column headers differ from the canonical names (e.g., 'total money' instead of 'revenue'), CIVORA's preview screen highlights the discrepancies. Assign columns manually or rely on CIVORA's semantic match engine. 3. Preprocessing: The Python task parses, cleans (removing bad characters, casting numbers), aggregates by dimensions, and updates database records. 4. Reload: Ingested figures are committed, and the view updates. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 04 Data Dictionary
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Data Dictionary Comprehensive Database Schema and File Schema Specification 1. Input CSV/Excel Column Specifications * Date: YYYY-MM-DD. Maps transaction timing. Crucial for trend lines. * Category: String (e.g., 'Electronics'). Determines product classification. * Region: String (e.g., 'Karnataka'). Used for regional distribution metrics. * Revenue: Decimal. Total amount collected. * Cost: Decimal. Raw acquisition cost. * Quantity: Integer. Number of items sold. * Store (Optional): String. If present, used to route imports to specific stores. 2. Database Table: users * id: INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY. Unique user identifier. * name: VARCHAR(255). Full name of user. * email: VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE. Authentication email. * password: VARCHAR(255). Bcrypt hashed password. * position: VARCHAR(255). User role/title (default 'Administrator'). * created_at: TIMESTAMP. Account creation time. 3. Database Table: projects * id: INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY. Unique store identifier. * user_id: INT. Foreign key mapping back to users. * name: VARCHAR(255). Custom store name. * store_type: VARCHAR(255). Franchise, warehouse, online, etc. * default_tax_rate: DECIMAL(10, 2). Default local tax percentage. * low_stock_threshold: INT. Inventory notification limit. 4. Database Table: sales_summaries * id: INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY. * project_id: INT. Linked project ID. * month_name: VARCHAR(50). E.g., 'January', 'February'. * year: INT. E.g., 2024. * total_revenue: DECIMAL(15, 2). * total_cost: DECIMAL(15, 2). Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 05 Business KPIs Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Business KPIs & Metrics Guide A Master Reference of Calculations, Formulations, and Decision Definitions 1. Gross Revenue Definition: The total value of sales transactions before any deductions. Formula: Gross Revenue = Sum(Revenue) of all transactions. Impact: Measures scale and top-line growth. It indicates sales volume traction. 2. Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Definition: The total cost incurred in acquiring or manufacturing items sold. Formula: COGS = Sum(Cost) of all transactions. Impact: Critical for measuring supply-chain efficiency and vendor cost control. 3. Net Contribution (Net Revenue) Definition: The absolute margin generated by sales after subtracting the raw costs. Formula: Net Contribution = Gross Revenue - COGS Impact: Represents money available to cover fixed administrative costs, marketing, and taxes. 4. Net Profit Margin (%) Definition: Profitability ratio that measures the percentage of revenue remaining after costs. Formula: Net Margin = (Net Contribution / Gross Revenue) * 100 Impact: Key metric for performance benchmarks. Margins under 15% indicate cost pressure; margins over 25% signify healthy operation. 5. Revenue Growth Rate (%) Definition: The period-over-period percentage change in revenue. Formula: Growth Rate = ((Current Period Revenue - Previous Period Revenue) / Previous Period Revenue) * 100 Impact: High growth indicates market expansion, while negative growth flags seasonal contraction or competitive churn. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 06 Data Visualization Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Data Visualization Guide How to Read, Interact with, and Configure Dashboard Visualizations 1. Metric Indicator Cards (KPIs) Positioned at the top of the main screen, these cards show: Total Revenue, Total Contribution (Profit), Market Hubs, and Units Sold. How to Read: Look for trend indicators. Units sold and total revenue should grow in tandem. Divergence indicates price compression or high costs. 2. Composed Trend Chart (Bar & Line) Visualizes monthly revenue (blue bars) and net profit (amber line) over time. Interactivity: Hovering reveals exact values. It helps spot seasonal peaks (e.g., high sales in Q4) and margins at a glance. 3. India Market Hubs (Geographic Map) Renders regional distribution nodes across Indian states (e.g. Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu). Visual Cues: Circle markers and popups identify hubs. The size of the marker correlates with regional sales contribution, helping highlight key geographic zones. 4. Category Mix (Donut Chart) Shows sales split across categories (Electronics, Furniture, Groceries, Apparel, Stationery). Strategic Action: Diversifying the donut sectors reduces reliance on a single product segment, protecting the business from category-specific drops. 5. Store Performance Breakdown Lists stores sorted by revenue velocity. Drilldowns: Clicking on a store in the list filters the regional map and KPI cards to reflect that store's isolated datasets. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 07 Forecasting Predictive Analytics Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Forecasting & Predictive Analytics Guide Methodology Behind Growth Forecasting and AI Conversational Summaries 1. Trend-Based Revenue Forecasting CIVORA calculates next-period revenue forecasts based on historical sales velocity. Formula: Next Revenue = Current Revenue * (1 + (Growth Rate / 100)). Fallback logic: If growth rate cannot be calculated (e.g., first month of data), a default baseline growth rate of 8.0% (0.08 multiplier) is applied. Best Practice: Upload at least three consecutive months of data for reliable trend mapping. 2. AI Chatbot Architecture CIVORA features an AI panel powered by Watsonx Orchestrate, with a local rule-based fallback system. The AI reviews dashboard context (aggregate statistics, regional trends, category mix, and year filters) to answer user questions. 3. Local Conversational Fallback Engine If the AI server is offline, the local fallback processes user text using keyword matching: * 'report' / 'summary' queries: Returns a text report highlighting consolidated revenue, profit, units sold, and the latest period's revenue. * 'compare' / 'vs' queries: Calculates the growth rate between the first and last uploaded months and provides growth metrics. * General queries: Provides system help, prompting users on how to ask about metrics, charts, or periods. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 08 Data Cleaning Preprocessing Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Data Cleaning & Preprocessing Guide How the Ingestion Engine Validates and Transforms Raw Files 1. Semantic Column Mapping Users often upload spreadsheets with inconsistent headers (e.g. 'qty', 'units', 'counts'). CIVORA uses a semantic dictionary to automatically map files: * Product: 'item', 'name', 'product', 'goods', 'article' * Revenue: 'revenue', 'price', 'sales', 'earnings', 'income', 'total money' * Cost: 'cost', 'expense', 'expenses', 'outlay', 'spending' * Quantity: 'quantity', 'qty', 'count', 'amount', 'volume', 'units' * Region: 'region', 'area', 'location', 'state', 'city', 'place' 2. Regional State Normalization Spelling discrepancies can break map visualizations. CIVORA maps region names to canonical Indian states using 'state_aliases.json': * E.g., 'Tamilnadu', 'TN', 'tamil nadu' -> 'Tamil Nadu' * E.g., 'mumbai', 'bombay', 'Maharashtra' -> 'Maharashtra' If no match is found, the value is title-cased. 3. Data Type Casting and Safety * Numeric conversion: Revenue, cost, and quantity columns are parsed using pandas.to_numeric(). Non-numeric entries (e.g., 'NA', '-', '$') are converted to 0. * Missing categories: Null categories default to 'General'. * Missing products: Null product names are handled, defaulting to 'N/A' or skipped. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 09 Error Codes Troubleshooting Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Error Codes & Troubleshooting Guide System Alerts, Database Recovery, and Setup Debugging Procedures 1. File Upload Errors * Error: 'Missing columns: Product, Revenue...' Cause: The uploaded file is missing required columns. Either map headers during import or rename headers in the source file. * Error: 'No file uploaded' Cause: File upload request received without file content. Verify browser settings. 2. Database Connection Errors * Error: 'ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3306' Cause: Backend cannot connect to the MySQL database. Restart the DB container: 'docker-compose restart db'. Wait 5 seconds and reload. * Error: 'Duplicate entry ... for key sales_summaries.project_id' Cause: Uploading data for a month/year that already exists. CIVORA automatically overwrites the old month's summary with new figures. 3. Application Docker Failures * Problem: Frontend won't load on http://localhost:3000. Solution: Verify docker state: 'docker-compose ps'. Check frontend logs: 'docker-compose logs web'. Confirm port 3000 is not in use by another app. * Problem: 'Port 3306 already in use'. Solution: Stop local MySQL servers running outside Docker before starting the platform. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 10 Sample Dataset Documentation
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Sample Dataset Documentation Reference Guidelines for Included Test Data Files 1. Overview of SAMPLE_DATA.csv This test file is located in the 'sample-test-data/' directory. It contains 31 transaction rows representing sales for January 2024. Metrics Overview: * Total rows: 31 * Target Year/Month: January, 2024 * Total Revenue represented: ~1,798,000 INR * Categories included: Electronics, Furniture, Others * Regions represented: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Telangana, Gujarat, Delhi, Kerala, Punjab, Haryana 2. Overview of HEATMAP_TEST_DATA.csv A smaller dataset designed for testing map coordinates and product-level drilldowns. It includes columns for specific product names (e.g. 'Alpha Phone', 'Beta Desk', 'Gamma Chair'). * Regions: Tamilnadu (mapped to Tamil Nadu), Kerala, Delhi, Orissa, Karnataka. * Value Range: Revenue spans from 50,000 to 120,000 INR. Use this file to test custom column mappings. 3. Verification Steps To test the system: 1. Select Month = January, Year = 2024. 2. Import 'SAMPLE_DATA.csv'. 3. Confirm that the dashboard updates with 11 active regional hubs, ~1.79M in total revenue, and correct category splits. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 11 Report Generation Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Report Generation Guide Operational Guide to Executive PDF Exporting and SWOT Summarization 1. Executive PDF Reports CIVORA provides a reporting module under the 'Reports' dashboard tab. It aggregates data into clean, executive-friendly summaries. Users can download these reports as PDF files. The export includes charts and SWOT analysis details. 2. SWOT Logic & Derivation * Strengths: Highlights the top-performing sales category and region based on total revenue contribution. * Weaknesses: Flags cost pressures if cumulative profit margins fall below 15%, or highlights high category concentration if sales are limited to a single segment. * Opportunities: Estimates next-period revenue based on growth rates and suggests replicating successful regional strategies. * Threats: Flags declining performance if growth rates are negative, and prompts review of inventory and tax configurations. 3. Exporting PDF Reports 1. Navigate to 'Reports'. 2. The system fetches and aggregates data across all active projects. 3. Review the SWOT analysis and trend summaries. 4. Click 'Download PDF' to generate the report file. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 12 Feature Documentation
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Feature Documentation Detailed Guide to CIVORA Capabilities 1. User Administration & Security CIVORA supports secure user authentication. Register using the registration form. Passwords are encrypted with bcrypt, and session authorization uses JWT (JSON Web Tokens) with a 7-day expiration. 2. Multi-Store / Multi-Project Framework Manage different retail outlets or business segments from a single account. Each store maintains isolated datasets, logos, and local tax settings. 3. Schema-Aware Data Ingestor Ingest Excel and CSV files without rigid layout requirements. The system maps columns semantically, normalizes regional spelling variations, and handles numeric casting and missing values. 4. Interactive Analytics Dashboard View trends with interactive charts, explore regional distribution on the India map, and analyze product categories via donut visualizations. 5. AI Assistant & Report Engine Analyze datasets using natural language queries. Generate PDF reports containing summaries, SWOT analysis, and trend visualizations. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 14 Privacy Policy
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION CIVORA Privacy Policy Data Privacy and Processing Regulations 1. Local-First Design Principle CIVORA is designed with a local-first architecture. All database storage and parsing happen on your local system or within private networks. CIVORA does not share your raw sales data. 2. Hashing and Authentication Data User credentials are encrypted using bcrypt. Session tokens (JWT) are stored securely in browser local storage and transmitted via authorization headers. 3. Third-Party AI Data Processing If you use the Watsonx Orchestrate chatbot, dashboard metrics are transmitted to the configured API. No raw file records or user passwords are sent. 4. Data Control and Deletion You have full control over your data. Deleting a project removes its sales records and summaries from the database. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION CIVORA Terms of Service Standard Usage Agreement and Licensing Rules 1. chunks.title: 16 Data Security Retention
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Data Security & Retention Policy Policies on Data Security and Cleanup 1. Database Infrastructure Security CIVORA uses MySQL 8.0 with Docker volume mapping. Database credentials must be configured securely in the environment file. 2. Session Security (JWT) Authentication uses JWT with HS256 signing. Tokens expire after 7 days, requiring users to re-authenticate. 3. Data Cleaning Policy Users can clear imported records using the dashboard settings. Deleting a store cleans up all related records in MySQL. 4. File System Cleanup Uploaded files are deleted from the backend server immediately after processing to prevent storage leakage. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 17 Business Analytics Glossary
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Business Analytics Glossary Definitions of Terms Used in the CIVORA Platform 1. Aggregation The process of consolidating multiple transaction rows into single figures (e.g., total monthly revenue) to analyze trends. 2. Margin The ratio of net profit to gross revenue, indicating the efficiency of sales operations. 3. Preprocessing Cleaning and formatting raw datasets prior to analysis, including state name normalization. 4. SWOT Analysis A framework for evaluating Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats based on business data. 5. Trend Line A visual indicator on charts representing the direction of sales performance over time. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 18 AI Features Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION AI Features Guide Overview of AI Integration, Chat Assistant, and Automated Insights 1. chunks.title: 19 API Documentation
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION CIVORA REST API Documentation Developer Guide to Integration and API Usage 1. Authentication Endpoints * POST /api/auth/register: Create a user account. * POST /api/auth/login: Authenticate and receive a JWT token. 2. Project & Store Endpoints * GET /api/projects: List projects associated with the user account. * POST /api/projects: Add a project. * PATCH /api/projects/:projectId: Update project properties. 3. Data Import & Dashboard Endpoints * POST /api/upload: Upload files. * GET /api/dashboard/summary: Fetch global aggregated statistics. * GET /api/dashboard/:projectId: Fetch details for a specific store. * DELETE /api/dashboard/:projectId: Clear store sales data. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential

chunks.title: 20 Administrator Guide
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Administrator Guide System Configuration, Permissions, and Deployment Guide 1. Account Roles & Multi-Tenancy Users default to the 'Administrator' role. Multi-tenancy is enforced at the database level: users can only view and manage projects they created. 2. Database Administration The database schema is initialized using 'init_db.sql'. Backup volume mappings are defined in 'docker-compose.yml'. 3. Deploying in Production Before deploying, change the default JWT secret and database passwords, configure SSL, and use production-ready web servers. chunks.title: 22 Limitations System Constraints
chunks.text: CIVORA DATA VISUALIZATION PLATFORM OFFICIAL KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENTATION Known Limitations & Constraints Overview of Technical Boundaries 1. Scale and File Size Limits Imports are processed synchronously on the backend. Files larger than 25MB may time out. For large datasets, split files by week or region. 2. Schema Inconsistencies Files must contain the five core columns: date, category, region, revenue, and quantity. Missing columns will cause validation errors. 3. Map Visualization Constraints The map visualization is centered on Indian states. Regional names that cannot be mapped will default to title case and will not render on the map. Page 1 | CIVORA Enterprise Documentation - Confidential
